title: When do Refugees Return Home? Evidence from Syrian Displacement in Mashreq
Economic Issues Related to Asian Deforestation
venue: Oxford Research Encyclopedia of Environmental Science
abstract:
The loss of Asian forests represents one of the most significant changes in contemporary land cover. Between 2000 and 2020 alone, an area twice the size of Malaysia has lost its tree cover as measured by Earth observation data. These trends have significant repercussions for greenhouse gas emissions, carbon storage, the conservation of biodiversity, and the wellbeing of Indigenous Peoples and local communities (IPLCs), making Asian deforestation a phenomenon of global concern.
There are many immediate factors that drive deforestation across Asia, but the conversion to commodity agriculture is the leading cause. Most notably, the expansion of oil palm and rubber plantations by both multinational corporations and smallholders has led to dramatic conversion of forests. The production of timber as well as pulp and paper has further contributed to significant deforestation, with the evolution of each sector often driven by government policies, such as logging bans.
However, it is the underlying drivers (i.e., distal and proximate causes) that determine where and when commodity production displaces forest cover. They are particularly challenging to tackle in a globalized world, where consumption patterns driven by local population and income growth lead to environmental and social change in distant producer countries, including in Asia. Certification programs and legality requirements have been put in place to address these externalities with varying success. Deforestation in Asia is also facilitated by weak governance and regulatory frameworks, where forest rights are often unclear, and financial, technological, and human resources for forest monitoring are limited.
Several contemporary forest governance strategies seek to promote sustainable management of Asian forests. Financial mechanisms such as reducing emissions from deforestation and forest degradation (REDD+) and payments for ecosystem services (PES) schemes seek to provide economic incentives for forest conservation. Pledges and activities to remove deforestation from commodity supply chains seek to respond to consumer demand, promote corporate environmental and social responsibility, and reduce the extent to which commodity supply chains contribute to Asian deforestation. And multiple state-led initiatives across Asia to empower IPLCs aim to align forest management objectives between national governments, subnational administrations, and local people. Assessing the impact of interventions related to financial mechanisms, corporate responsibility, and local forest governance will be critical to shaping the future of Asian forest cover change.
abstract_zh:
亚洲森林的减少是当代土地覆被最显著的变化之一。仅在2000年至2020年间，依据地球观测数据测算，相当于两个马来西亚面积的土地失去了树木覆盖。这些趋势对温室气体排放、碳储存、生物多样性保护以及原住民和当地社区（Indigenous Peoples and local communities, IPLCs）的福祉具有重大影响，使亚洲森林砍伐成为一个具有全球关注度的现象。
驱动亚洲森林砍伐的直接因素有很多，但向商品农业的转换是首要原因。尤为突出的是，跨国公司和小农户对油棕和橡胶种植园的扩张，导致了森林的大规模转化。木材生产以及纸浆和造纸业也进一步造成了大量森林砍伐，而这些行业的演变往往受到政府政策（如伐木禁令）的驱动。
然而，正是深层驱动因素（即远端和近端原因）决定了商品生产在何时何地取代森林覆盖。在全球化的世界中，这些因素尤其难以应对：当地人口和收入增长所驱动的消费模式，导致了遥远生产国（包括亚洲国家）的环境与社会变化。认证计划和合法性要求已经建立，以应对这些外部性问题，但成效参差不齐。亚洲的森林砍伐还受到治理薄弱和监管框架不完善的助长，其中森林权利往往不清晰，用于森林监测的财政、技术和人力资源也十分有限。
当代若干森林治理策略旨在促进亚洲森林的可持续管理。诸如减少毁林和森林退化所致排放（REDD+）以及生态系统服务支付（PES）计划等金融机制，旨在为森林保护提供经济激励。将森林砍伐从商品供应链中剔除的承诺与行动，旨在回应消费者需求，促进企业履行环境与社会责任，并减少商品供应链对亚洲森林砍伐的推动作用。此外，亚洲各国多项由政府主导的赋权IPLCs的举措，旨在使国家政府、地方行政机构与当地民众之间的森林管理目标保持一致。评估与金融机制、企业责任以及地方森林治理相关的干预措施的影响，对于塑造亚洲森林覆盖变化的未来至关重要。

title: Supporting pathways to prosperity in forest landscapes - A PRIME framework
abstract: We develop a framework to conceptualize the multiple ways forests contribute to poverty reduction and inform development interventions in forest landscapes. We identify five key strategies for reducing poverty in forest landscapes: a) improvements in productivity (P) of forest land and labor; b) governance reform to strengthen community, household and women’s rights (R) over forests and land; c) investments (I) in institutions, infrastructure and public services that facilitate forest-based entrepreneurship; d) increased access to markets (M) for timber or non-timber forest products; and e) mechanisms that enhance and enable the flow of benefits from forest ecosystem services (E) to the poor. We test the utility of the framework through a review of the forestry portfolio of the World Bank Group, the largest public investor in forestry. Many of these projects include several, but not all, PRIME components. We devote particular attention to forest-related investments in two contrasting countries, Vietnam and Mexico, to examine synergies among the pathways. Results suggest that each strategy in the PRIME framework may play an important role in alleviating poverty, but pronounced impacts may require multiple pathways to be jointly pursued. The PRIME framework can guide research to address knowledge gaps on pathways to prosperity in forest landscapes, serve as an easily remembered checklist for managers, and nudge forest program designers in government and development organizations, who are interested in poverty reduction, to focus on the importance of both a comprehensive framework and synergies across different pathways.
abstract_zh: 我们构建了一个框架，用以概念化森林对减贫的多种贡献方式，并为森林景观中的发展干预提供参考。我们确定了森林景观减贫的五项关键策略：a）提高森林土地和劳动力的生产率（P）；b）推进治理改革，以加强社区、家庭以及妇女对森林和土地的权利（R）；c）投资于有助于森林相关创业的制度、基础设施和公共服务（I）；d）增加获得木材或非木质林产品市场的机会（M）；以及e）增强并促成森林生态系统服务（E）惠益流向贫困人口的机制。我们通过回顾世界银行集团（全球最大的公共森林投资者）的林业项目组合，检验了该框架的效用。其中许多项目包含了PRIME框架的若干（但并非全部）组成部分。我们特别关注越南和墨西哥两个情况截然不同的国家的森林相关投资，以考察各路径之间的协同效应。结果表明，PRIME框架中的每一项策略都可能在减贫中发挥重要作用，但要产生显著影响，可能需要共同推进多条路径。PRIME框架可以指导研究，弥补森林景观中通往繁荣之路的知识空白；可作为管理者易于记忆的核查清单；并促使关注减贫的政府及发展机构的项目设计者，重视全面框架以及不同路径之间协同效应的重要性。

title: A systematic map of evidence on the contribution of forests to poverty alleviation
abstract:
Forests provide an essential resource to the livelihoods of an estimated 20% of the global population. The contribution of forest ecosystems and forest-based resources to poverty reduction is increasingly emphasized in international policy discourse and conservation and development investments. However, evidence measuring the effect of forest-based activities on poverty outcomes remains scattered and unclear. Lack of systematic understanding of forest-poverty relationships, in turn, inhibits research, policymaking, and efficient financial resource allocation.
To identify relevant studies for inclusion in this systematic map we searched six bibliographic databases, 15 organizational websites, eight systematic evidence syntheses (reviews and maps), and solicited information from key informants. Search results were screened for relevance against predefined inclusion criteria at title, abstract, and full text levels, according to a published protocol. Included articles were coded using a predefined framework. Trends in the evidence, knowledge gaps and relatively well-researched sub-topics are reported in a narrative synthesis. Occurrence and extent of existing evidence about links between interventions and outcomes are presented in a visual heatmap. Data are available through the open access Evidence for Nature and People Data Portal (
http://www.natureandpeopleevidence.org
).
A total of 242 articles were included in the systematic map database. Included articles measured effects of 14 forest-based intervention types on 11 poverty dimensions. The majority of the evidence base (72%) examined links between productivity-enhancement strategies (e.g. forest management, agroforestry, and habitat management) and monetary income and/or social capital outcomes. Other areas with high occurrence of articles include linkages between interventions involving governance, individual rights/empowerment or linked enterprises/livelihood alternatives with impacts on monetary income from direct sale of goods. A key knowledge gap was on the impacts of investment-based interventions (i.e. enhancing produced, human, and social capitals). Another was the impacts of forest-based interventions on financial capital (savings, debt), non-monetary benefits, and health.
The evidence base on forest-based productive activities and poverty alleviation is growing but displays a number of biases in the distribution of articles on key linkages. Priorities for future systematic reviews and evaluations include in-depth examinations into the impacts of rights-based activities (e.g. governance, empowerment) on poverty dimensions; and productivity-enhancing activities on social capital. More comprehensive and robust evidence is needed to better understand the synergies and trade-offs among the different objectives of forest conservation and management and variation in outcomes for different social groups in different social-ecological contexts.
abstract_zh:
全球约20%的人口的生计依赖于森林，森林为其提供了不可或缺的资源。在国际政策讨论以及保护与发展投资中，森林生态系统及森林资源对减贫的贡献日益受到重视。然而，衡量森林活动对贫困结果影响的证据仍然零散且不清晰。缺乏对森林与贫困关系的系统性认识，进而阻碍了研究、政策制定以及有效的财政资源配置。
为了在本系统图谱中纳入相关研究，我们检索了六个文献数据库、15个机构网站、八项系统性证据综合（综述和图谱），并向关键信息提供者征集信息。检索结果依照已发表的研究方案，根据预先设定的纳入标准在标题、摘要和全文层面进行筛选。纳入的文献使用预先定义的框架进行编码。证据的趋势、知识空白以及研究较为充分的子主题，以叙述性综合的方式进行报告。干预与结果之间联系的证据出现情况和程度，则以可视化热图呈现。数据可通过开放获取的“自然与人类证据数据门户”（Evidence for Nature and People Data Portal，http://www.natureandpeopleevidence.org）获取。
系统图谱数据库共纳入242篇文献。纳入的文献衡量了14种森林干预类型对11个贫困维度的影响。大部分证据基础（72%）考察的是生产力提升策略（例如森林管理、农林复合经营和栖息地管理）与货币收入和/或社会资本结果之间的联系。其他文献数量较多的领域，包括治理、个人权利/赋权或关联企业/生计替代方案等干预与直接销售商品所带来的货币收入之间的联系。一个关键的知识空白在于投资型干预（即增强生产性、人力和社会资本）的影响。另一个空白则是森林干预对金融资本（储蓄、债务）、非货币收益以及健康的影响。
关于森林相关生产活动与减贫的证据基础正在增长，但在关键联系的文献分布上仍存在若干偏差。未来系统综述和评估的优先方向包括：深入考察权利导向型活动（例如治理、赋权）对各贫困维度的影响；以及生产力提升型活动对社会资本的影响。需要更全面、更稳健的证据，以更好地理解在不同社会—生态背景下，森林保护与管理的不同目标之间的协同与权衡，以及不同社会群体的结果差异。

title: What is the evidence for the contribution of forests to poverty alleviation? A systematic map protocol
abstract:
Forests provide an essential resource that support the livelihoods of an estimated 20% of the global population. Forests are thought to serve in three primary roles to support livelihoods: subsistence, safety nets, and pathways to prosperity. While we have a working understanding of how poor people depend on forests in individual sites and countries, much of this evidence is dispersed and not easily accessible. Thus, while the importance of forest ecosystems and resources to contribute to poverty alleviation has been increasingly emphasized in international policies, conservation and development initiatives and investments—the strength of evidence to support how forests can affect poverty outcomes is still unclear. This study takes a systematic mapping approach to scope, identify and describe studies that measure the effect of forest-based activities on poverty outcomes at local and regional scales. This effort builds upon an existing systematic map on linkages between conservation and human well-being in order to make this process more efficient. We will conduct a refined and updated search strategy pertinent to forests-poverty linkages to glean additional evidence from studies outside the scope of the original map. Results of this study can be used for informing conservation and development policy and practices in global forest ecosystems and highlight evidence gaps where future primary studies and systematic reviews can add value.
We build upon the search strategy outlined in McKinnon et al. (Environ Evid 1–25, 2016) and expand our search to cover a total of 7 bibliographic databases, 15 organizational websites, 8 existing systematic reviews and maps, and evidence gap maps, and solicit key informants. All searches will be conducted in English and encompass all nations. Search results will be screened at title, abstract, and full text levels, recording both the number of excluded articles and reasons for exclusion. Full text assessment will be conducted on all included article and extracted data will be reported in a narrative review that will summarize trends in the evidence, report any knowledge gaps and gluts, and provide insight for policy, practice and future research. The data from this systematic map will be made available as well, through an open access, searchable data portal and visualization tool.
abstract_zh:
全球约20%的人口的生计依赖于森林，森林为其提供了重要资源。一般认为，森林在支撑生计方面发挥三种主要作用：维持生存（subsistence）、社会安全网（safety nets）以及通往繁荣的路径（pathways to prosperity）。虽然我们对贫困人口在个别地点和国家如何依赖森林已有一定的工作性认识，但大部分证据较为分散，不易获取。因此，尽管国际政策、保护与发展倡议和投资中越来越强调森林生态系统和资源对减贫的贡献，但森林活动如何影响贫困结果的证据强度仍不明确。本研究采用系统图谱方法，对在地方和区域尺度上衡量森林活动对贫困结果影响的研究进行界定、识别和描述。本研究建立在已有的一份关于保护与人类福祉之间联系的系统图谱基础之上，以提高该过程的效率。我们将开展经过修订和更新的检索策略，专门针对森林与贫困之间的联系，以从原图谱范围之外的研究中获取额外证据。本研究的结果可用于为保护与发展政策和实践提供参考，并突出那些需要未来开展原始研究和系统综述加以填补的证据空白。
我们以McKinnon等人（Environ Evid 1–25, 2016）提出的检索策略为基础，并扩大检索范围，涵盖七个文献数据库、15个机构网站、8项现有系统综述和图谱及证据空白图谱，并征集关键信息提供者。所有检索均以英文进行，覆盖所有国家。检索结果将在标题、摘要和全文层面进行筛选，同时记录被排除的文献数量及排除原因。对所有纳入文献进行全文评估，提取的数据将在叙述性综述中报告，以总结证据趋势，报告知识空白和过剩之处，并为政策、实践和未来研究提供参考。该系统图谱的数据还将通过开放获取、可检索的数据门户和可视化工具公开提供。

title: The Political Economy of Deforestation in the Tropics
abstract: Tropical deforestation accounts for almost one-fifth of greenhouse gas emissions worldwide and threatens the world's most diverse ecosystems. The prevalence of illegal forest extraction in the tropics suggests that understanding the incentives of local bureaucrats and politicians who enforce forest policy may be critical to understanding tropical deforestation. We find support for this thesis using a novel satellite-based dataset that tracks annual changes in forest cover across eight years of institutional change in post-Soeharto Indonesia. Increases in the numbers of political jurisdictions are associated with increased deforestation and with lower prices in local wood markets, consistent with a model of Cournot competition between jurisdictions. Illegal logging increases dramatically in the years leading up to local elections, suggesting the presence of "political logging cycles".And, illegal logging and rents from unevenly distributed oil and gas revenues are short run substitutes, but this effect dissapears over time as political turnover occurs. The results illustrate how incentives faced by local government officials affect deforestation, and provide an example of how standard economic theories can explain illegal behavior.
abstract_zh: 热带毁林占全球温室气体排放的近五分之一，并威胁着世界上最具多样性的生态系统。热带地区非法的森林采伐十分普遍，这表明理解执行森林政策的地方官员和政治人物的激励机制，对于理解热带毁林可能至关重要。我们利用一个新颖的卫星数据集支持了这一论点，该数据集追踪了苏哈托下台后印度尼西亚八年制度变革期间森林覆盖的年度变化。政治辖区数量的增加与毁林增加以及当地木材市场价格下降相关，这与辖区之间古诺竞争的模型相一致。在地方选举前的数年，非法伐木显著增加，表明存在“政治伐木周期”。此外，非法伐木与分配不均的石油和天然气收入所产生的租金在短期内是替代品，但随着政治更替的发生，这一效应会逐渐消失。这些结果说明了地方政府官员面临的激励如何影响毁林，并提供了一个例子，表明标准经济理论可以解释非法行为。
